entries.title: Match Cut
entries.text:
Match Cut

Plant and payoffChekhov’s gun

A match cut joins two shots through a visual, spatial, sonic, or conceptual correspondence the viewer can read at the splice. The outgoing frame and the incoming frame share a shape, motion, object class, or idea, so the cut argues a relationship instead of only changing the view.

Volume

Create this Match Cut

Narrative function

One side of the join is complete. The other side is complete.

What they share is the point: a bone leaving a hand, then a craft in the same screen path; a match blown out, then a sun the same size in the frame. The splice is the sentence.

Use it when two images are the same idea and you want that idea to land in one frame of time. It is the wrong tool when you only need a new camera position on the same gesture: that job belongs to match on action, and forcing a rhyme will feel like decoration.

If the second image does not change what the first one meant, skip the trick. A contour rhyme with no conceptual load is a graphic match wearing a bigger name.

How it works

Design both frames as a pair before either is shot. Match the dominant contour, screen position, motion vector, or sonic envelope, then cut hard.

There is no optical mix: A is 100 percent, then B is 100 percent, and the correspondence is what the viewer supplies in the gap. Keep the shared property honest.

A door that sticks in the first shot must stick for the same mechanical reason later. Prompt both sides: name the outgoing object, the incoming object, the shared geometry or motion, and a hard cut, not a morph.

When to use it

Use it at the leap: tool to tool, flame to sun, a planted object returning with a new meaning. Do not use it as a pretty way to leave a room.

If the next shot is only the next room, a straight cut or a Dissolve is cleaner.

Compared with similar shots

A graphic match rhymes form (shape, line, color, placement) even when the idea is thin. A match cut can use that rhyme, but it needs a correspondence of meaning, space, or sound as well.

Match on action stays inside one continuous gesture and hides the camera change. Match Motion rides a vector into another place or time.

Morph interpolates pixels; a match cut does not.

Graphic MatchForm carries you across time.

Match on ActionHide the cut in a movement.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

In film

In 2001: A Space Odyssey the thrown bone is followed by an orbiting craft on a related path, tool to tool across eras. In Lawrence of Arabia a blown match is followed by the desert sun at matching scale.

Apocalypse Now binds ceiling fan and helicopter so the two rotors share a thought. Use those joins as grammar, not as frames to copy.

Back to the Future 1985The clock-tower information becomes crucial to the climax.

Shaun of the Dead 2004Ordinary objects and earlier remarks become survival tools and jokes.

Parasite 2019Objects and architectural details accumulate later significance.

Lawrence of Arabia 1962A match being extinguished is followed by the desert sunrise.

2001: A Space Odyssey 1968Bone and spacecraft associate different technological eras.

Pulp Fiction 1994Interlocking episodes are presented outside chronological order.

Once Upon a Time in America 1984Different periods of life are woven together.

Prompt it

Write both sides of the join. Example: Match cut from [Subject] to a rhyming shape or motion in another time, graphic continuity across a hard cut, bone to station.

Name the shared contour or vector, name what changes (place, era, scale), and forbid a morph or dissolve. For video, generate A and B as separate shots with matched screen position, then cut; do not ask the model to blend them.

Use in Video Generator

In an early workshop scene, casually show a door that sticks unless lifted slightly. Later, during an urgent evacuation, a visitor fails to open it until the apprentice remembers the trick. Generate the same door hardware and motion in both scenes. Avoid a conspicuous explanatory close-up in the setup.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a morph or a graphic match with nothing to say. The tell is identical subject identity with no shared geometry, or a liquid melt from A into B.

The fix: lock the shared contour, placement, or motion; keep the two objects distinct; cut hard.

Questions

What is Match Cut in film?

A match cut is an edit that connects two complete shots through a visual, spatial, sonic, or conceptual correspondence. Both sides of the join are readable on their own; the splice is what claims they belong together.

Match Cut vs Graphic Match

A graphic match is a form rhyme: silhouette, circle, line, or color in the same screen place. A match cut may use that rhyme, but it also carries an idea, a space, or a sound from one side of the join to the other.

When should I use Match Cut?

Use it when two images are the same thought and the cut should make that thought visible. Do not use it to paper over a missing camera position on one action.

How do I prompt Match Cut for AI image or video?

Describe shot A, shot B, the shared shape or motion, and a hard cut. Example: Match cut from [Subject] to a rhyming shape in another time, bone to station. Say no morph and no dissolve.

entries.title: Graphic Match
entries.text:
Graphic Match

Shape matchRaccord graphique

A graphic match cut joins two images that share a dominant shape, line, color, placement, or motion pattern, even when location and time change. The outgoing contour and the incoming contour occupy the same part of the screen, so form carries you across the splice.

Volume

Create this Graphic Match

Narrative function

You leave a drain, circular, centered. You arrive on an eye, circular, centered.

Nothing has been explained, but the cut has already made a bridge. The viewer feels the leap before anyone names it.

Use it when form should carry you across time or place. It is the wrong tool when the two frames do not share a contour you can point at.

Matching wardrobe or actor identity is not a graphic match. A graphic match is not a morph.

Similarity across a hard cut is enough. If the image melts, you have left editing and entered morph.

How it works

Design the outgoing and incoming frames together. Match the important contour and screen position rather than every part of the image: circle size, horizon height, the diagonal of a body.

Use a hard cut when the instant connection is the point. A short Dissolve can soften the rhyme, but it also hides how precise the match was.

Prompt the silhouette or the echoed shape on both sides, same placement, no morph.

When to use it

Use it when a silhouette, a circle, or a line should survive a jump in time: a watch face to a dome, a scream-mouth to a tunnel. Do not use it as wallpaper between unrelated wides.

If the contour does not match, the cut is just a cut.

Compared with similar shots

A Match Cut may include a graphic rhyme, but it also claims an idea. Graphic match can be purely formal.

Match on Action continues one gesture in one scene. Dissolve overlaps two images in time instead of snapping form to form.

Morph interpolates; graphic match does not.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

Match on ActionHide the cut in a movement.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

In film

2001: A Space Odyssey throws a bone and finds a craft of similar attitude and screen path. Psycho leaves the shower drain and arrives on Marion's eye, two circles in one place.

Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown uses compositional rhymes to connect successive images. Borrow the geometry, not the posters.

2001: A Space Odyssey 1968The thrown bone is followed by an orbiting spacecraft.

Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown 1988Compositional similarities connect successive images.

Prompt it

Graphic match on the silhouette of [Subject], shape echoing shape, circle to circle, a visual rhyme. Specify the shared contour, its screen position, and that the objects stay distinct.

For video: generate A and B with the same dominant shape size and placement, then hard-cut. No morph, no dissolve unless you explicitly want a soft rhyme.

Use in Video Generator

Generate A: close-up of a circular watch face centered in frame. Generate B: a circular observatory dome seen from above at exactly the same size and position. Hard-cut on the shared circle, with no morph or dissolve. Keep the two objects distinct and the visual connection immediate.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is morph or a lazy Match Cut that only repeats the actor. The tell: the model blends A into B, or the second frame does not occupy the same contour.

The fix: lock one shape and one placement, keep two different objects, cut hard.

Questions

What is Graphic Match in film?

A graphic match is a cut that connects images with similar shape, line, color, placement, or movement pattern. The two sides of the join can be different places and times; the shared form is the bridge.

Graphic Match vs Match Cut

Graphic match is a form rhyme. Match cut is a correspondence that can include form but also idea, space, or sound. Many famous joins are both; the graphic match name is about the contour, not the thesis.

When should I use Graphic Match?

Use it when form should carry the viewer across a leap in time or place. Do not use it when the two frames share no readable contour.

How do I prompt Graphic Match for AI image or video?

Name the silhouette or shape on both sides and put it in the same screen place. Example: Graphic match on the silhouette of [Subject], circle to circle. Demand a hard cut and two distinct objects.

entries.title: Match on Action
entries.text:
Match on Action

Cut on movementRaccord mouvement

Match on action cuts during one continuous action so the movement itself bridges two camera positions. The outgoing shot starts the gesture; the incoming shot finishes it, which is why the edit can change size or angle without feeling interrupted.

Volume

Create this Match on Action

Narrative function

A hand reaches for a handle in a wide. In the close shot the same hand, same speed, same sleeve, finishes the turn.

The viewer follows the reach instead of inspecting the splice. That is the job: hide the cut in a movement.

It is the wrong tool when the action is not continuous, or when you want the skip to be seen. Skipping time inside a similar frame is a Jump Cut.

Jumping closer on the same axis without a bridging gesture is an Axial Cut. If hands swap, travel reverses, or too much of the motion is repeated on both sides, the glue fails and the cut becomes visible for the wrong reason.

How it works

Repeat the action with matching speed, hand, object position, and body orientation. Cut at a readable phase of motion, usually the acceleration or the midpoint, not after the gesture has already landed.

Check screen direction and sound continuity across the join. The two sides are the same event, different views.

Prompt: the motion started in one shot and finished in the next, same hand, same object, two framings.

When to use it

Use it to change shot size or angle on a door, a punch, a sit-down, a pour. Do not use it to leap to another day or another room.

If the world changes while the vector continues, that is Match Motion, not match on action.

Compared with similar shots

A Match Cut rhymes two different images. Match on action is one action, two views.

An Axial Cut jumps distance on the same axis and does not need a bridging gesture. Match Motion can carry a body into another location or reality if direction and speed match.

Invisible Cut hides the splice in occlusion or blur, not in a readable gesture.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

Axial CutChange shot size without changing angle.

Graphic MatchForm carries you across time.

In film

Buster Keaton's Neighbors connects courtyard movement across changing views so the body remains the through-line. The Matrix links action across changing shot sizes and viewpoints while the gesture continues.

Classical continuity comedy and action both depend on this glue. Use the principle, not a copied punch.

Neighbors 1920Keaton’s courtyard movement is connected across shots.

The Matrix 1999Action is linked across changing shot sizes and viewpoints.

Prompt it

Match on action through [Subject]'s gesture, the motion started in one shot and finished in the next. Name the wide and the close, the hand, the object, the direction of travel, and that the cut happens during the move.

For video, generate A and B of the same reach or step, then cut mid-motion. Do not reverse the hand or the walk.

Use in Video Generator

Generate A: wide view of a courier reaching for a door handle with the right hand. Generate B: close view from the same side of the action axis, continuing that exact reach and turning the handle. Cut during the reach, preserving hand, speed, sleeve and handle position.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Jump Cut (time skipped, similar frame) or an Axial Cut (scale jump, no bridging move). The tell: the close shot uses the other hand, the walk flips screen direction, or the gesture completes twice.

The fix: match hand, speed, object, orientation; cut during the move, not after.

Questions

What is Match on Action in film?

Match on action is a cut made during one continuous gesture so movement bridges two camera positions. One side starts the action; the other side finishes it.

Match on Action vs Match Cut

Match on action stays inside one event and hides a change of view. A match cut joins two different images that correspond in form, space, sound, or idea.

When should I use Match on Action?

Use it when you need a new size or angle on the same ongoing move: a door, a hit, a sit. Do not use it to skip time or change location.

How do I prompt Match on Action for AI image or video?

Describe a gesture started in one framing and finished in the next. Name the hand, the object, and the cut during motion. Example: Match on action through [Subject]'s gesture, continuity glue.

entries.title: Jump Cut
entries.text:
Jump Cut

Visible temporal discontinuityFaux raccord temporel

A jump cut removes time or slightly shifts framing inside a similar setup, so the discontinuity is conspicuous. The outgoing frame and the incoming frame are close enough that the missing interval reads as a skip, not as a new shot.

Volume

Create this Jump Cut

Narrative function

The car is the same. The road is the same.

The speaker has jumped three sentences and a mile. You are not soothed.

The film has shown the skip. Use it for impatience, instability, comic abbreviation, or an openly constructed voice.

It is the wrong tool when you want invisible continuity. If the two frames are very different in size or angle, the skip hides and you have ordinary coverage, not a jump cut.

A jump cut is not simply any fast cut. The visible break within a similar setup is the whole point.

How it works

Remove intervals from one setup, or join closely related views of the same subject. Keep enough of the composition (lens, angle, body size) that the jump is obvious.

Decide whether sound smooths the skip (a continuous line) or emphasizes it (hard in and out). Prompt: time skipped inside a similar framing, same seat, missing frames, no morph.

When to use it

Use it in a wait, a rambling talk, a comedown, a drive that should feel too long and too short at once. Do not use it as a substitute for coverage you did not shoot.

If the audience should not notice the edit, use Match on Action or an Invisible Cut.

Compared with similar shots

A Smash Cut slams into a violently different image. A jump cut stays inside a similar frame and skips time.

Montage juxtaposes many shots to compress or argue; jump cut is usually one setup with holes. An Axial Cut jumps distance on the same axis as emphasis, not as missing time.

Quick Cuts are short shots from changing setups, a rhythm, not a skip inside one frame.

Smash CutThe next image should hurt.

MontageYou need months in a minute.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Breathless lets car rides and talks skip forward inside similar framings, which is the modern template. Dancer in the Dark uses discontinuous cutting to disrupt smooth observation.

Requiem for a Dream turns repeated rituals into jumps that feel like appetite. Grammar, not a look to clone.

Breathless 1960Car rides and conversations skip forward within similar framings.

Dancer in the Dark 2000Discontinuous cutting disrupts smooth observation.

Prompt it

Jump cut on [Subject], time skipped inside a similar framing, interruption, anxiety or comedy of missing frames. Specify a locked or near-locked setup, what changes (posture, clock, crowd), and that the camera does not morph.

For video, one bench or seat, several jumps, elapsed waiting, no repositioning disguised as a jump.

Use in Video Generator

Locked medium shot of a woman waiting at a station bench. Make six jump cuts in the same framing as she changes posture, checks the clock and shifts her bag. Other passengers change between cuts. Clear elapsed waiting time, no morphing transitions or camera repositioning.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Quick Cuts or random coverage labeled as a jump. The tell: every shot is a new angle, so nothing jumps.

Or the model morphs the sitter from pose to pose. The fix: keep the framing nearly constant, remove time, let the discontinuity show.

Questions

What is Jump Cut in film?

A jump cut removes time while leaving enough similarity of framing or subject that the break is obvious. Both sides of the join look like the same shot with a hole in it.

Jump Cut vs Smash Cut

A jump cut skips time inside a similar setup. A smash cut leaves that setup for a violently different image, sound, or scale. One shows a hole; the other shows a collision.

When should I use Jump Cut?

Use it when the skip itself is the meaning: wait, nerves, comic speed, a narrator who will not pretend the cut is invisible. Do not use it to hide missing coverage.

How do I prompt Jump Cut for AI image or video?

Keep one framing and skip time inside it. Example: Jump cut on [Subject], time skipped inside a similar framing. Name what changes between jumps and forbid morphing.

entries.title: Smash Cut
entries.text:
Smash Cut

Apparent closureLast-beat reversal

A smash cut makes an abrupt, high-contrast transition in image, sound, tone, scale, or time. The outgoing side has earned a state (quiet, prayer, resolution); the incoming side contradicts it without a polite blend.

Volume

Create this Smash Cut

Narrative function

A night walk tightens. A bus door hisses into the frame.

The scare was a vehicle, not a monster, and the cut is the joke and the slap at once. Or: a grave visit settles, then a hand breaks the earth.

The next image should hurt. Use it when contrast is the meaning.

It is the wrong tool when the two sides are similar, or when you still need the audience inside one continuous action. Similar frames with missing time are a Jump Cut.

A few stolen frames of another image are a Flash Cut. Earn the first state.

A smash from nowhere, with no quiet or no prayer, is only loud.

How it works

Hold A long enough to establish tone, scale, or apparent closure. Cut to B with a large change in brightness, loudness, shot size, or subject class: silence to noise, interior to blast, hymn to murder.

No dissolve, no fade, no matched contour unless the match is itself the insult. Coordinate picture and sound so they smash together, or delay the sound for a second smash (the blast seen, then heard).

Prompt: from [Subject] to a violently different image, no polite dissolve.

When to use it

Use it at the false ending, the bus in the dark, the cut from a kiss to a siren. Do not use it on every scene change.

If nothing in A was quiet, sacred, or resolved, B has nothing to smash.

Compared with similar shots

A Jump Cut stays in a similar frame and skips time. A Crash Cut is a hard collision used as percussion or as a start inside an event; smash cut is contrast after a state has been earned.

A Match Cut rhymes; smash cut usually refuses the rhyme. Cross-Cutting alternates lines over time; smash is one brutal join.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

Graphic MatchForm carries you across time.

In film

Cat People uses the bus to interrupt a tense walk: the cut is the scare and its release. Carrie lets the aftermath settle, then destabilizes the coda.

Whiplash smashes quiet into the kit. Oppenheimer lets the Trinity flash arrive before the blast sound.

Contrast as grammar, not a shot to duplicate.

Carrie 1976The apparent aftermath and grave visit lead to a final destabilizing event.

Oppenheimer 2023The Trinity explosion is experienced visually before the full blast sound arrives.

Cat People 1942The bus interrupts the tense nighttime walk.

The Exorcist III 1990The hospital corridor sequence uses prolonged observation before a sudden attack.

Alien 1979Jones the cat provides an apparently threatening sound or movement with an innocent explanation.

Cat People 1942The approaching bus resolves one immediate expectation of attack.

Prompt it

Smash cut from [Subject] to a violently different image, silence to noise, prayer to explosion, no polite dissolve. Name the outgoing state (quiet, dark, small, resolved) and the incoming opposite (loud, bright, huge, ruptured).

For video, hold A, then hard-cut to B; specify the sound smash or the delayed boom.

Use in Video Generator

After a conservator returns a stolen painting, show a calm closing sequence: gallery reopened, lights dimmed, doors locked. In one final locked shot, reveal a tiny fresh brushstroke appearing on the otherwise restored canvas. Keep the event subtle and consistent with earlier clues, not an unrelated shock.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Dissolve (polite) or a Jump Cut (same setup). The tell: A and B have similar brightness, scale, and tone, so nothing smashes.

The fix: earn a state on A, change at least two axes (sound and scale, or tone and time) on B, cut hard.

Questions

What is Smash Cut in film?

A smash cut is an abrupt, high-contrast join in image, sound, tone, scale, or time. One side of the splice has a state; the other side breaks it without a blend.

Smash Cut vs Jump Cut

A jump cut skips time inside a similar framing. A smash cut leaves that world for a violently different one. Similarity is the jump cut's tell; contrast is the smash cut's tell.

When should I use Smash Cut?

Use it when the next image should hurt after quiet, prayer, or false closure. Do not use it as a default scene change.

How do I prompt Smash Cut for AI image or video?

Name the earned state and the contradicting image. Example: Smash cut from [Subject] to a violently different image, silence to noise, no dissolve. Hold A, then hard-cut to B.

entries.title: Dissolve
entries.text:
Dissolve

cross-dissolveAudio match transitionSonic metamorphosis

A dissolve gradually overlaps the outgoing shot with the incoming shot so both images occupy the frame for a measurable duration. Opacity of A falls as opacity of B rises; at the midpoint you are looking at two ghosts.

Volume

Create this Dissolve

Narrative function

A face thins. A landscape thickens through it.

Time has passed, or memory has, and the cut did not want to be a door slam. Dissolves are for passage, recollection, or the gentle death of a scene.

It is the wrong tool when the next image should hurt, or when the correspondence should snap. Hurt is a Smash Cut.

Snap-rhyme is a Match Cut or Graphic Match. If you hold the overlap as a meaning in itself, you are in Double Exposure territory, not a transition.

A dissolve does not automatically mean years have passed. Duration, sound, and context do that work.

A two-frame dissolve is just a soft cut.

How it works

Mix A and B over time: typically a dozen frames to a few seconds. Keep a shared compositional hook if you want the overlap to read (a fan through a rotor, a face through a ceiling).

Decide whether sound dissolves with picture or bridges first. This is an optical or digital mix, not a camera move.

Prompt: dissolve from [Subject] into another time or place, overlapping ghosts, longer than a cut admits.

When to use it

Use it for memory, montage-like passage, or a scene that should die instead of stop. Do not use it to hide a bad match on action.

If the two sides should collide, cut hard.

Compared with similar shots

A Fade In / Fade Out goes to a uniform field (black or color) so there is a moment with no scene. A dissolve never empties the frame; B is already there.

Double Exposure holds two images as a stacked meaning, not as a handoff. Morph warps contours; dissolve only changes opacity.

Wipe uses a traveling boundary instead of a mix.

Fade In / Fade OutA scene is a book chapter.

Double ExposureTwo times or two selves occupy one frame.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Citizen Kane uses dissolves as time's grammar through a life. The Godfather lets faces and rooms bleed across turns of power.

Apocalypse Now layers hotel fan, jungle, and helicopter so picture and sound dissolve together. The 39 Steps bridges a scream into a train whistle, a sonic cousin of the mix.

Grammar of overlap, not a look to steal.

Apocalypse Now 1979Helicopter imagery and hotel-fan perception are linked through sound and image.

The 39 Steps 1935A scream is bridged into a train whistle.

The Stendhal Syndrome 1996The painting and subjective immersion are linked through overlapping images.

Apocalypse Now 1979The opening layers landscape, face and interior imagery.

Prompt it

Dissolve from [Subject] into another time or place, overlapping ghosts, a longer time than a cut admits. Name both images, a shared hook if any (shape, motion, sound), and the mix duration.

For video, two full shots plus an opacity crossfade; do not morph bodies or melt sets.

Use in Video Generator

End on an old projector turning in a dark room. Let its rhythmic mechanical chatter continue across a cut to a sewing workshop, then resolve naturally into the sewing machine now on screen. Generate both pictures separately and match the two sound rhythms without a decorative visual dissolve.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Fade In / Fade Out (empty field in the middle) or a morph. The tell: the frame goes to black, or A warps into B.

The fix: keep both pictures intact, change only opacity, let the midpoint show two readable images.

Questions

What is Dissolve in film?

A dissolve overlaps the outgoing shot with the incoming shot so both are visible for a duration. One side fades in presence while the other takes over; there is no empty field in between.

Dissolve vs Fade In / Fade Out

A fade goes to or from a uniform black or color field, a pause with no scene. A dissolve hands one picture to another through a mix. Fade punctuates; dissolve bleeds.

When should I use Dissolve?

Use it for memory, elapsed time, or a scene that should die softly. Do not use it when the next image should smash or when a hard graphic rhyme is the point.

How do I prompt Dissolve for AI image or video?

Name both shots and the overlap. Example: Dissolve from [Subject] into another time or place, overlapping ghosts. Specify a mix, not a morph, and how long the ghosts share the frame.

entries.title: Fade In / Fade Out
entries.text:
Fade In / Fade Out

Fade-outPunctuation through absence

A fade in or fade out takes the picture to or from a uniform field of black or color, rather than handing the frame straight to another visible scene. One side of the join is a world; the other side is absence, sleep, death, or a chapter break.

Volume

Create this Fade In / Fade Out

Narrative function

The room goes. Red remains, or black does, long enough to feel like a closed book.

Then another room is born from the same field. A fade is punctuation, not a mix of two stories.

Use it when a scene is a chapter, when consciousness drops, or when you want a pause the audience can rest in. It is the wrong tool for a gentle bleed between two images that should both stay present: that is a Dissolve.

It is also the wrong tool if you only want to point at a face inside a shrinking circle: that is an Iris. A fade does not automatically mean a long period has passed.

Sound that continues over black can mean a second of unconsciousness. Sound that dies with the picture can mean an ending.

How it works

Reduce the picture to a field (or raise a picture out of one). Choose black for neutral chaptering, or a color (deep red, white) when the field itself should feel like a mood.

Coordinate whether sound survives the empty picture. Do not fill the room with fog or smoke to fake a fade; the image must leave, not get weather.

Prompt: fade to or from black around [Subject], chapter punctuation, sleep, death, or the start of a world.

When to use it

Use it to open a film, close an act, or mark a blackout of awareness. Do not use it between every scene in a contemporary dialogue piece unless you want a period cadence.

If two pictures should overlap, dissolve.

Compared with similar shots

A Dissolve overlaps two scenes; a fade empties the frame first. An Iris is a moving mask that points at a detail while the rest goes black, not a full-field fade.

A Wipe keeps both pictures alive, divided by a traveling edge. Vignette is optical falloff on a living image, not a transition.

DissolveMemory, passage, or a gentle death of a scene.

IrisPoint with the mask itself.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Cries and Whispers uses red fields as emotional punctuation between rooms and crises. 1917 uses a blackout to separate lapse and return of consciousness.

Classical studio films chapter with fades to black as a default. Borrow the pause, not a tint as a trademark.

Cries and Whispers 1972Red transitions give the film a distinctive emotional punctuation.

1917 2019A blackout separates the protagonist’s lapse and return of consciousness.

Prompt it

Fade to or from black around [Subject], chapter punctuation, sleep, death, or the start of a world. Name the field color if it is not black.

For video, specify whether sound dies with the picture or hangs over the empty field. Do not describe smoke filling the room.

Use in Video Generator

A woman closes her eyes in a quiet room. Fade the image slowly into deep dark red while the room’s ticking continues for one second, then stops. Hold the empty color field before the next scene. Produce the fade and sound timing in post, not as red smoke filling the room.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Dissolve (two pictures mixed) or fog as a fake fade. ' The fix: go to a uniform field, hold it, then let the next scene emerge.

No overlap, no weather.

Questions

What is Fade In / Fade Out in film?

A fade takes the image to or from a uniform black or color field. One side of the join is a scene; the other is absence, not another picture mixed on top.

Fade In / Fade Out vs Dissolve

A dissolve overlaps two shots so both are visible at once. A fade inserts a field of black or color between worlds. Dissolve bleeds; fade punctuates.

When should I use Fade In / Fade Out?

Use it for chapter breaks, openings, endings, sleep, or a loss of consciousness. Do not use it as a blend between two images that should share the frame.

How do I prompt Fade In / Fade Out for AI image or video?

entries.title: Wipe
entries.text:
Wipe

horizontal wipevertical wipediagonal wipeclock wiperadial wipebarn-door wipeshape wipeDirectional replacement

A wipe replaces one image with another through a moving boundary that travels across the frame. One side of the join is still A; the other side is already B; the edge between them is the edit, and it is meant to be seen.

Volume

Create this Wipe

Narrative function

A vertical line walks left to right and a village becomes a mountain pass. Geography has changed as a page turn, not as an invisible cut.

Adventure, serials, and playful maps like that honesty. Use it when the change of scene should feel brisk, storybook, or openly constructed.

It is the wrong tool when you need the audience not to feel an edit: that is Invisible Cut or Match on Action. A wipe is not a person walking in front of the lens (occlusion).

Occlusion can hide a cut; a wipe displays one. Direction and speed should agree with the next action.

A wipe against the traveler's walk fights the grammar.

How it works

Choose a boundary: vertical, horizontal, diagonal, clock hand, barn-door, shape. Animate it across a clean pair of shots.

Soft-edged or hard-edged is a taste choice; the edge must remain a graphic, not a morph of the scenery. A motivated object edge (a passing wall, a cloak) can justify a wipe, but then you are close to an invisible occlusion cut.

Prompt: wipe replacing [Subject] with the next image, a line traveling across the frame, a clock hand or a hard vertical.

When to use it

Use it to leap from planet to planet, village to road, chapter to chapter in a serial cadence. Do not use it to hide a continuity error.

If the join should vanish, do not wipe.

Compared with similar shots

An Iris is a radial mask from a center, not a traveling edge. A Match Cut rhymes two full frames with a hard cut and no boundary.

A Dissolve mixes opacities. An Invisible Cut uses a real object or blur to conceal the splice; the wipe's graphic boundary is intentional and visible.

IrisPoint with the mask itself.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

Graphic MatchForm carries you across time.

In film

Star Wars uses directional wipes as adventure punctuation between locations. Seven Samurai uses wipes to mark narrative progression with a visible page-turn.

Those are grammar samples for an honest scene change, not compositions to clone.

Star Wars 1977Directional wipes connect adventure scenes and locations.

Seven Samurai 1954Wipes punctuate narrative progression.

Prompt it

Wipe replacing [Subject] with the next image, a line traveling across the frame, Star Wars grammar or a clock hand. Name direction, edge hardness, and both scenes.

For video, generate A and B as full frames, then composite a moving mask. No blending scenery, no morph.

Use in Video Generator

Generate A: a traveler leaves a dusty village at dawn. Generate B: the traveler approaches a distant mountain pass later that day. Replace A with B using a clean left-to-right vertical wipe. Consistent travel direction, no blending or morphing scenery.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is an Invisible Cut (hidden occlusion) or a Dissolve. The tell: the edge is gooey, or a passing extra is doing the work while you call it a wipe.

The fix: a clean traveling mask, two intact pictures, direction matched to the story's travel.

Questions

What is Wipe in film?

A wipe replaces one shot with another through a moving boundary across the screen. Both sides of the join are full pictures; the traveling edge is the edit, and it is meant to be seen.

Wipe vs Iris

A wipe's edge travels (left to right, clock, barn-door). An iris is a circular or shaped mask that opens or closes around a center. One is a page turn; the other is a pointing hole.

When should I use Wipe?

Use it for adventure, serial geography, or a playful scene change that should not pretend to be invisible. Do not use it to hide a splice the audience must not feel.

How do I prompt Wipe for AI image or video?

Name both images and the traveling edge. Example: Wipe replacing [Subject] with the next image, a line traveling across the frame. Specify direction and a clean mask, not a morph.

Generate A: a traveler leaves a dusty village at dawn. Generate B: the traveler approaches a distant mountain pass later that day. Replace A with B using a clean left-to-right vertical wipe. Consistent travel direction, no blending or morphing scenery.

entries.title: Iris
entries.text:
Iris

Iris-inIris-out

An iris transition reveals or conceals the picture with a moving circular or shaped mask. The mask's center is a pointer: one side of the join is the full world, the other is a hole closing on a face, a detail, or black.

Volume

Create this Iris

Narrative function

The hall is there. The circle tightens on a satisfied face, then opens a little to include the yawning cat on the piano, then shuts.

Silent comedy pointed with the mask itself. The iris is a wink and a chapter ending at once.

Use it to isolate a comic detail, imitate a viewing device, or close in an openly theatrical way. It is the wrong tool if you only want the image to die evenly: that is a Fade In / Fade Out.

It is also not a zoom into a dark tunnel. The camera can sit still while the mask moves.

An iris is a mask over the image, not a Vignette. Vignette is optical falloff on a living frame.

Iris is a boundary that travels until the picture is gone or born.

How it works

Build the mask in post (or in-camera with an iris gimmick). Control center, shape, and timing.

Decide whether the circle follows a subject or stays fixed while action continues underneath. Iris-in opens from black; iris-out closes to black (or to a tiny remaining image).

Prompt: iris in or out on [Subject], a circular mask closing on a face or detail, silent-era pointing, or a wink.

When to use it

Use it to point at a ring, a glance, a gag, or to end a scene as theatre. Do not use it as a substitute for a push-in.

If the camera must physically approach, move the camera. If the world should fade as a whole, fade.

Compared with similar shots

A Fade In / Fade Out empties the whole field evenly. A Wipe uses a traveling straight or clock edge, not a hole from a center.

Vignette darkens corners without being a transition. A zoom changes focal length; the iris does not.

Match Cut joins two full frames; iris withholds the frame on purpose.

VignetteHold the eye in. Do not crush the sides as a filter.

Fade In / Fade OutA scene is a book chapter.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Neighbors uses a circular reveal to change the apparent scale and circumstances of a wedding. The Artist borrows silent-era punctuation, including iris-like framing, as a period grammar.

Silent comedy at large treated the iris as a pointing finger. Use the mask logic, not a pastiche overlay on every close-up.

Neighbors 1920A circular reveal changes the apparent scale and circumstances of the wedding.

The Artist 2011Silent-film-derived visual punctuation includes iris-like framing.

Prompt it

Iris in or out on [Subject], a circular mask closing on a face or detail, silent-era pointing, or a wink. Name the center (an eye, a ring, a cat), whether the mask follows, and whether it opens or closes.

For video, generate the clean scene, then animate a circular mask in post. Do not zoom into darkness and call it an iris.

Use in Video Generator

A violinist finishes a performance in an otherwise empty hall. Close a circular iris around her satisfied face, then let the circle reveal a tiny yawning cat on the piano before closing to black. Generate the clean scene and animate the mask separately.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a zoom, a Fade In / Fade Out, or a heavy Vignette. The tell: the camera pushes in, or the whole frame dims evenly, or corners are just dark.

The fix: keep the camera still, animate a circular mask with a chosen center, let the unmasked picture stay at full exposure.

Questions

What is Iris in film?

An iris is a moving circular or shaped mask that reveals or conceals part of the image. One side of the join is the open picture; the other is a pointing hole, often closing to black.

Iris vs Fade In / Fade Out

A fade takes the entire image to a uniform field. An iris keeps a chosen center visible while the mask closes or opens. Fade is a chapter; iris is a finger.

When should I use Iris?

Use it to point at a detail, end a gag, or quote silent-era punctuation. Do not use it when you mean a zoom or an even fade to black.

How do I prompt Iris for AI image or video?

Name the subject and the mask. Example: Iris in or out on [Subject], a circular mask closing on a face or detail. Specify center and direction (in or out), and say it is a mask, not a zoom.

entries.title: Cross-Cutting
entries.text:
Cross-Cutting

Misleading cross-cutWrong-door suspense

Cross-cutting alternates two or more locations or action lines, often implying they are happening at the same time. Each side of the join is a complete strand; the engine is meanwhile, two clocks racing.

Volume

Create this Cross-Cutting

Narrative function

A baptism in one room. Killings in others.

The film does not wait for one to finish. It braids them so ritual and murder share a tense.

Or: a team at a door, a listener at another door, and the cut teaches you they are about to meet until a reverse proves they are not. Use it when simultaneity, comparison, or false geography is the engine.

It is the wrong tool when you need one compressed idea from unlike images: that is Montage. It is also the wrong tool when two rooms must be visible at once: that is Split Screen.

Fair misdirection relies on inference. Do not show matching house numbers and then pretend the doors were different.

How it works

Shoot each line so it can be interrupted: clear geography, readable time of day or clock, compatible but not identical details if you plan a wrong-door surprise. Alternate with tightening duration if you want the clocks to race.

Sound can bleed across (a bell, a vow) to bind the lines. Prompt: cross-cutting between [Subject] and a simultaneous other line, suspense by alternation, two clocks racing.

When to use it

Use it for a raid versus a doorbell, a ritual versus a crime, dream levels that must tick together. Do not use it to dump unused coverage of one scene.

If there is no second clock, you are just cutting.

Compared with similar shots

Montage collides images to make an argument or to compress months; cross-cutting keeps parallel actions alive. A Smash Cut is one contrast join, not a braid.

Split Screen shows both lines at once instead of alternating. An L-cut lets sound from one line sit on the picture of the other without changing the picture's location.

MontageYou need months in a minute.

Smash CutThe next image should hurt.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

The Godfather baptizes Michael while the rival killings land in other rooms. The Silence of the Lambs intercuts an FBI raid with a doorbell, then reveals the geography was wrong.

Inception alternates dream levels so one clock pressures another. Use the braid, not the blocking.

The Silence of the Lambs 1991The FBI raid is intercut with the killer’s doorbell before the geography is revealed.

The Godfather 1972The baptism is intercut with the killings of Michael’s rivals.

Inception 2010The climax alternates between dream levels.

Prompt it

Cross-cutting between [Subject] and a simultaneous other line, suspense by alternation, two clocks racing. Name both geographies, what the viewer is invited to assume, and whether that assumption is true.

For video, two distinct spaces, alternating shots, tightening duration. Do not morph one room into the other.

Use in Video Generator

Generate A: a team approaches a building and presses a doorbell. Generate B: someone in a similar interior hears a bell and walks toward a door. Intercut as though they connect. Reveal in a wide reverse that B opens to a lone courier at a different address. Keep the earlier shots ambiguous rather than contradictory.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Montage (idea by collision) or Split Screen (both at once). The tell: the second line has no clock, or both lines are clearly the same hallway.

The fix: two geographies, implied simultaneity, a reveal if you are lying about the door.

Questions

What is Cross-Cutting in film?

Cross-cutting alternates locations or action lines, usually to imply they are simultaneous. Each side of the join is its own strand; the cut says meanwhile.

Cross-Cutting vs Montage

Montage juxtaposes shots to compress time or produce an idea. Cross-cutting keeps two (or more) ongoing actions in play and braids them. One argues; the other races clocks.

When should I use Cross-Cutting?

Use it when two lines must tick together: raid and doorbell, vow and murder, two escapes. Do not use it as a pile of unused singles from one room.

How do I prompt Cross-Cutting for AI image or video?

Name both spaces and the race. Example: Cross-cutting between [Subject] and a simultaneous other line, two clocks racing. Keep the geographies distinct and the assumption of contact clear.

Generate A: a team approaches a building and presses a doorbell. Generate B: someone in a similar interior hears a bell and walks toward a door. Intercut as though they connect. Reveal in a wide reverse that B opens to a lone courier at a different address. Keep the earlier shots ambiguous rather than contradictory.

entries.title: Split Screen
entries.text:
Split Screen

Rashomon structureReplayed encounter

Split screen shows two or more image fields at once, so separate spaces share a single moment on the same frame. Both sides of the join are visible together; there is no waiting for the next cut.

Volume

Create this Split Screen

Narrative function

A phone call places two apartments in one picture. A party splits into the night you wanted and the night you got.

Dual identity, dual time, or dual witness: the pane is the grammar. Use it when two rooms must be one moment, or when comparison is the joke.

It is the wrong tool when the audience should assume contact and then be wrong: that surprise is often better as Cross-Cutting. It is also not a window, doorway, or mirror inside the set.

That is Frame within Frame, a diegetic frame, not a panel. Replaying an event from another angle does not automatically make the accounts unreliable.

Split screen can show agreement as easily as a lie.

How it works

Shoot or generate each pane with matched eye-lines, horizon, or motion if you want the split to feel like one organism (a Match Split). Or keep the panes frankly separate for a phone call.

Decide the boundary: hard vertical, architectural, torn. Keep identity stable unless the point is two versions of one person.

Prompt: split screen with [Subject] in one pane and another life in the other, simultaneous spaces, phone-call cinema or dual identity.

When to use it

Use it for simultaneous phone calls, twins, expectation versus reality, four quadrants of one hour. Do not use it as wallpaper on a single conversation that wants ordinary coverage.

If you need the second room later, cut later.

Compared with similar shots

Cross-Cutting alternates; split screen co-presents. Frame within Frame is a picture found in the world (a window, a phone, a doorway).

Match Split is a split whose dividing line or contour continues from one world into the other. Montage sequences images; split screen stacks them now.

Frame within FrameSomeone is watched, trapped, or pictured.

Cross-CuttingMeanwhile is the engine.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Pillow Talk and other studio comedies park two ends of a phone call in one frame. Timecode runs four continuous views in quadrants.

Kill Bill and Sisters use panels as simultaneous action. (500) Days of Summer splits expectation and reality at a party.

Use the pane logic, not a copied poster.

Rashomon 1950Testimonies offer incompatible versions of the central encounter.

Elephant 2003Paths and encounters are revisited from different students’ viewpoints.

Jackie Brown 1997The money exchange is replayed through different participants’ perspectives.

Carrie 1976The prom catastrophe uses simultaneous panels.

Sisters 1972Separate fields of action share the screen.

Pillow Talk 1959Telephone conversations place separated people together.

Timecode 2000Four continuous camera views occupy four screen quadrants.

Napoléon 1927The finale expands into a triptych in its Polyvision presentation.

(500) Days of Summer 2009The party is divided into expectations and reality.

Prompt it

Split screen with [Subject] in one pane and another life in the other, simultaneous spaces, phone-call cinema or dual identity. Name the boundary, whether eyelines match, and what each pane contains.

For video, two (or more) complete shots composited, not one image torn as a texture.

Use in Video Generator

Show one lost-wallet incident three times: from the owner’s view, a cleaner’s view and a distant passenger’s view. Preserve the same station clock, movements and wallet position, but reveal different occluded actions each time. The third version resolves the apparent theft without inventing a new event.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Frame within Frame (a real window) or Cross-Cutting (sequential). The tell: a doorway in the set, or the model giving you one wide with a scratch down the middle.

The fix: two fully directed spaces, a graphic divide, simultaneous time.

Questions

What is Split Screen in film?

Split screen shows multiple image fields at once. Both sides of the join occupy the frame together, so two rooms or two versions share one moment.

Split Screen vs Cross-Cutting

Cross-cutting alternates lines so you see one, then the other. Split screen presents them simultaneously. Alternation creates meanwhile; panels create co-presence.

When should I use Split Screen?

Use it when two spaces must be one moment: a call, twins, expectation versus reality. Do not use it as a substitute for a window in the set or for ordinary coverage.

How do I prompt Split Screen for AI image or video?

Describe each pane and the divide. Example: Split screen with [Subject] in one pane and another life in the other, simultaneous spaces. Specify a hard boundary and two complete scenes.

entries.title: Montage
entries.text:
Montage

Associative juxtapositionIdea generated by the cut

Film montage creates meaning or compression through the ordered juxtaposition of shots. Each side of a join is a complete image; the claim lives in the order, the collision, or the months squeezed into a minute.

Volume

Create this Montage

Narrative function

Workers, then a slaughterhouse. The cut is an argument.

Or: sweat, rope, steps, a breath, the same stairs later, a body that can now climb. Time has collapsed, and the sequence did the climbing.

Use it when you need months in a minute, or an idea neither image holds alone. It is the wrong tool when two ongoing actions must remain simultaneously alive: that is Cross-Cutting.

It is the wrong tool when you only want to skip a few seconds in one setup: that is a Jump Cut. An evocative analogy is not factual proof.

Do not let the sequence imply unsupported real-world causation.

How it works

State the intended inference or the time curve first. Choose images whose relation is legible: matching geometry for analogy, progressive sizes or sweat for training, repeated rituals for addiction.

Control duration as a metric (shortening toward a peak, or a held pause as payoff). Prompt: montage sequence built around [Subject], time collapsed by images, training, travel, or a life in twenty shots.

When to use it

Use it for training, a marriage dying over breakfasts, a city arriving, an essay of images. Do not use it to cover a scene you could have played in continuity.

If the audience must follow one fight blow by blow, shoot the fight.

Compared with similar shots

Cross-Cutting braids parallel actions that continue. Montage often finishes each shot as a unit in an argument or a time-lapse of life.

Jump Cut holes out one setup. Fragments withhold a complete view of one event; montage may show complete views whose collision is the event.

Quick Cuts are a duration pattern; they become montage when the order makes a claim.

Cross-CuttingMeanwhile is the engine.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Rocky and The Karate Kid compress training into progressive labor. Strike and October collide images into political argument.

Citizen Kane breakfasts a marriage down to silence. Up condenses a life into selected moments.

Steal the function (compress, argue), not the needle-drops.

October 1927Religious images are combined into an overt visual argument.

Yi Yi 2000The father’s and daughter’s dates are linked across different places and experiences.

The Godfather 1972Religious vows and violence are juxtaposed in the baptism passage.

Up 2009The married-life passage condenses years into selected moments.

Citizen Kane 1941The breakfast sequence compresses changes in a marriage.

Traffic 2000Party fragments omit time and destabilize experience.

Rocky 1976Training progresses toward the run up the museum steps.

The Karate Kid 1984Repetitive tasks are reframed as skill-building.

Requiem for a Dream 2000Repeated consumption rituals are compressed into extreme-detail fragments.

Shaun of the Dead 2004Everyday preparation is accelerated through emphatic inserts.

Hot Fuzz 2007Travel and administrative procedures become rapid visual punctuation.

Prompt it

Montage sequence built around [Subject], time collapsed by images, training, travel, or a life in twenty shots. List the ordered images, what the collision claims, and whether time or idea is the engine.

For video, many distinct shots, no morph between them, a duration curve. Do not ask for one tracking shot labeled montage.

Use in Video Generator

Match recurring barriers and mechanical rhythms to suggest institutional organization, while keeping humans visibly individual. No captions asserting the analogy as an objective fact.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Quick Cuts with no claim, or a single moving camera. The tell: twenty angles of the same five seconds, or a morphing collage.

The fix: pick an inference or a time span, choose distinct images, cut on order, let the join do the work.

Questions

What is Montage in film?

Montage is meaning or compression made by the order of shots. Each side of a join is a picture; the idea appears in the juxtaposition, not in either image alone.

Montage vs Cross-Cutting

Cross-cutting keeps two action lines running in implied simultaneity. Montage compresses duration or collides images to make a claim. One races clocks; the other builds an argument or a month.

When should I use Montage?

Use it when you need months in a minute, or an idea that only exists between images. Do not use it as a pile of unused coverage from one scene.

How do I prompt Montage for AI image or video?

List the shots and the claim. Example: Montage sequence built around [Subject], time collapsed by images, training, travel, or a life in twenty shots. Specify order, not a single moving take.

entries.title: Axial Cut
entries.text:
Axial Cut

Jump along the camera axisCut-in emphasis

An axial cut jumps closer or farther along approximately the same camera axis, changing shot size without changing angle. The outgoing frame and the incoming frame share a viewpoint; only distance snaps.

Volume

Create this Axial Cut

Narrative function

A farmhouse kitchen, then the same kitchen larger, then an eye socket you were not ready to occupy. Recognition arrives as a series of shocks, not as a walk.

Change shot size without changing angle. Use it for stepwise emphasis: a date in a book, a wound, a face that must suddenly fill the world.

It is the wrong tool when you want a continuous approach. A Crash Zoom In is an optical move in time.

A dolly-in is a walk. An axial cut is an edit.

If the angle changes more than a few degrees, you have ordinary coverage, not an axial cut. If time is what you skipped inside one size, you have a Jump Cut.

How it works

Capture or generate matched wide, medium, and close compositions on the same axis. Preserve pose, eyeline, and background alignment enough that the jump is only scale.

Choose deliberate steps (for example 50mm at 3 meters, then 50mm at 1 meter, or a punch-in crop that matches a true closer camera). Do not animate a zoom between the frames if the point is the snap.

Prompt: axial cut jumping toward or away from [Subject] along the lens axis, punch-in without a zoom.

When to use it

Use it when a detail must land as a blow: the date stamp, the empty eye, the gun on the table. Do not use it as a substitute for a motivated push-in during a long take.

If the camera should walk, walk.

Compared with similar shots

A Crash Zoom In is a continuous, fast focal-length change. An axial cut is a splice.

A Jump Cut skips time in a similar size; axial cut skips distance on one axis. Match on Action needs a bridging gesture; axial cut can hit a still figure.

A push-in has parallax; a punch-in crop of one take has none, and is a cheaper cousin of a true closer camera on the same axis.

Crash Zoom InPunctuate a hit, a realization, or a comic sting.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

The Birds sends Lydia through successive closer views of the dead farmer, the axis held, the scale jumping. The Shining uses hard axial emphasis on rooms and faces so space feels like a trap.

Goodfellas punches in for recognition rather than a polite zoom. Use the snap, not a copied kitchen.

The Birds 1963Lydia’s discovery of the dead farmer is emphasized through successive closer views.

Prompt it

Axial cut jumping toward or away from [Subject] along the lens axis, punch-in without a zoom, a snap of scale. Name two or three matched framings, same angle, same pose, hard cuts.

For video, do not ask the model to zoom; ask for a cut between a wide and a close on the same axis.

Use in Video Generator

A librarian notices an impossible new date stamped inside an old book. Make three hard cuts on the same axis: desk-wide, book close-up, extreme close-up of the date. Keep the page and hands fixed, with no zoom animation, morph or lateral angle change. Add exact date text in compositing.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a Crash Zoom In or a digital crop sold as a camera move. The tell: the lens breathes, or the angle walks off axis, or the subject morphs larger.

The fix: two (or three) still-matched compositions, same axis, hard cuts, pose locked.

Questions

What is Axial Cut in film?

An axial cut jumps closer or farther along the same camera axis. Both sides of the join share an angle; only shot size changes, as a snap rather than a move.

Axial Cut vs Crash Zoom In

A crash zoom is a continuous optical move. An axial cut is an edit between matched distances on one axis. One is a whoosh; the other is a punch.

When should I use Axial Cut?

Use it to change shot size without changing angle, when recognition should shock. Do not use it when you want the camera to walk or the lens to zoom in time.

How do I prompt Axial Cut for AI image or video?

Ask for matched wide and close frames on the same axis, then a hard cut. Example: Axial cut jumping toward [Subject] along the lens axis, punch-in without a zoom. No zoom animation.

Invisible Cut

Substitution spliceStop trick

An invisible cut hides an edit through motion, darkness, occlusion, blur, matching geometry, or digital stitching. One side of the join and the other are meant to feel like a single take; the splice is a seam the audience should not find.

Volume

Create this Invisible Cut

Narrative function

A coat fills the lens. When it leaves, the room is later, or the body is gone, or the street has changed.

You needed a cut the audience must not feel. Stop-trick cinema did this with a locked camera and a substitution.

Contemporary oners do it with whips, walls, and stitches. Use it to simulate a long take, to vanish a person, or to change time inside an apparently continuous walk.

It is the wrong tool when the cut should be a sentence: a Match Cut, a Smash Cut, a Wipe. If you want the join seen, do not hide it.

The trick depends on spatial continuity around the substitution. A wandering unmatched camera exposes an unintended jump.

How it works

Plan a hiding place: a passing body, a dark wall, a whip-pan blur, a matched doorway, a digital stitch on a texture. Lock exposure and lighting across plates if you are substituting.

For a stop trick, lock the camera, hold actors, change the object, splice on the occlusion. For an oner illusion, match motion blur and grain at the whip.

Prompt: invisible cut hidden in [Subject]'s whip, a dark wall, or a passing body, the oner illusion.

When to use it

Use it to extend a take through a theatre, a trench, a street, or to make a woman vanish from a chair. Do not use it to avoid writing a scene change.

If the geography actually transforms as you watch, that may be a Set Transition instead of a hidden splice.

Compared with similar shots

A Oner is the long take you are faking or actually shooting. A Whip Pan can be the bandage over the splice.

Match on Action hides a cut in a readable gesture but still changes the view on purpose. Set Transition lets the location rewrite itself.

Morph is a visible interpolation, the opposite of invisible.

OnerThe scene is a ride.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

The Vanishing Lady substitutes a seated woman between frames. A Trip to the Moon pops Selenites out of existence.

Rope hides joins in dark foregrounds. 1917 and Birdman stitch walks so trenches and theatres feel continuous.

Spectre's opening presents multiple spaces as one shot. Grammar of concealment, not a take to clone.

The Vanishing Lady 1896A seated woman apparently disappears and is replaced.

A Trip to the Moon 1902Selenites disappear in bursts when struck.

1917 2019Long continuous-looking stretches through trenches, ruins and open ground.

Birdman 2014The theatre and city passages appear to flow continuously despite time shifts.

Rope 1948Dark foreground surfaces conceal some joins between long takes.

Spectre 2015The opening Day of the Dead passage presents multiple spaces as an apparently continuous shot.

Rope 1948Dark foreground bodies help conceal selected joins.

1917 2019Objects, darkness and motion help maintain continuous-looking travel.

Prompt it

Invisible cut hidden in [Subject]'s whip, a dark wall, or a passing body, the oner illusion. Name the hiding action, the before plate, the after plate, and that the camera path should appear continuous.

For video, two plates joined at occlusion or blur; locked lighting; no liquid morph.

Use in Video Generator

A stage magician drops a cloth over an empty chair. At the instant the cloth fills the chair silhouette, cut to an identically framed plate with a bouquet beneath it. The magician lifts the cloth. Locked camera, matching hands and shadows, no liquid morph or camera move. Generate two plates and join them at the occlusion.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a visible Whip Pan that never hides a join, or a morph. The tell: a pop in grain, a jump in crowd, a morphing wall.

The fix: a true occluder or blur that fills the frame, matched lighting, a hard splice inside that fill, continuous motion on both sides.

Questions

What is Invisible Cut in film?

An invisible cut hides the edit in motion, darkness, occlusion, blur, matching geometry, or stitching. Both sides of the join are meant to play as one continuous shot.

Invisible Cut vs Oner

A oner is a long take. An invisible cut is how you fake or extend one: the splice sits inside a whip, a wall, or a passing body. One is the apparent shot; the other is the seam.

When should I use Invisible Cut?

Use it when the audience must not feel the edit: a vanishing act, a stitched walk, a time jump inside a continuous-looking path. Do not use it when the join should speak.

How do I prompt Invisible Cut for AI image or video?

Name the hiding place and both plates. Example: Invisible cut hidden in [Subject]'s whip, a dark wall, or a passing body. Demand matched lighting and no morph.

entries.title: J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup)
entries.text:
J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup)

Contrapuntal soundIronic music

A J-cut or L-cut visual setup is a picture designed so sound can lead or lag across the splice. One side of the join is a face, a room, or a listener that can hold; the other side is a space already speaking, or still speaking after we have left it.

Volume

Create this J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup)

Narrative function

We hear the next room before we see it (J-cut): the picture stays on the walker, the voice has already arrived. Or we see the listener while the speaker's words continue (L-cut): the face is the bridge.

Sound will lead or lag. The face is the bridge.

Use it when picture and track should not cut on the same frame, so thought can cross a doorway. It is the wrong tool when you need both rooms visible at once (Split Screen) or when you only need a mute reaction insert with no overlapping track.

Randomly mismatched music is not automatically meaningful counterpoint. Define what the lag reveals: dread, irony, a voice that will not let the face go.

How it works

On the timeline, a J-cut lets incoming audio start under the outgoing picture. An L-cut lets outgoing audio continue under the incoming picture.

The visual setup is a shot that can bear that overlap: a Reaction Shot, a walk toward a door, an empty office. Keep the sound's source clear enough that the overlap is information, not muddle.

Prompt: a frame of [Subject] designed as the picture half of an L-cut or J-cut, reaction holding while another space is already speaking.

When to use it

Use it to enter a conversation before the room, to stay on a listener after a confession, to let a song continue over a packing scene it does not belong to. Do not use it as default dialogue cutting if both faces should share the same on-camera words.

If you need meanwhile geography, Cross-Cutting.

Compared with similar shots

A Reaction Shot is the picture; J-cut and L-cut are how that picture meets sound. Cross-Cutting alternates whole lines.

A smash in sound on a picture cut is closer to Smash Cut. Counterpoint (cheerful music on a cruel image) can ride an L-cut, but the technique here is the staggered splice, not the playlist.

Reaction ShotThe important action is watching.

Cross-CuttingMeanwhile is the engine.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

The Social Network and Heat keep speech living over listeners' faces so thought continues across the join. The Conversation makes incoming sound a threat before the picture explains it.

Yi Yi lets piano arrive before its source is located. A Clockwork Orange and Reservoir Dogs place cheerful tracks against behavior the picture will not bless.

Use the stagger, not the needle-drop.

A Clockwork Orange 1971Cheerful performance is placed against disturbing behavior.

Reservoir Dogs 1992The radio song contrasts with the warehouse torture scene.

Yi Yi 2000Piano music is heard before its source is fully located visually.

Heat 1995Use the diner conversation to study speech continuing over a listener’s view; exact overlaps require an edition check.

Prompt it

A frame of [Subject] designed as the picture half of an L-cut or J-cut, reaction holding while another space is already speaking. For stills, describe a listening face or a doorway that can hold offscreen voice.

For video, specify whether audio of B starts under A (J) or audio of A continues under B (L), and name both spaces.

Use in Video Generator

A cheerful original corporate jingle plays over a spotless office being emptied after a sudden closure. Workers quietly pack plants and family photographs while the tune maintains its bright tempo. Generate restrained visual coverage and compose an original cue; do not imitate an existing recording or melody.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a mute Reaction Shot with picture and sound cutting together, or a Cross-Cutting that never overlaps track. The tell: lips in the new room are already talking in sync at the picture cut, with no pre-lap.

The fix: hold the first picture while the second track starts, or hold the first track after the picture has moved.

Questions

What is J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup) in film?

A J-cut starts the next shot's sound before its picture; an L-cut keeps the last shot's sound after the picture has changed. The visual setup is a frame that can hold while the other space speaks.

J-Cut / L-Cut vs Reaction Shot

A reaction shot is a picture of listening. J-cut and L-cut are how that picture is joined to another space's sound. You can have a reaction with a straight cut; the J/L is the stagger.

When should I use J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup)?

Use it when sound should lead a scene in, or linger after we have left. Do not use it if picture and track must hit together as a smash.

How do I prompt J-Cut / L-Cut (Visual Setup) for AI image or video?

Describe a face or room that can hold offscreen voice. Example: A frame of [Subject] as the picture half of an L-cut or J-cut, reaction holding while another space is already speaking. For video, say which track pre-laps.

entries.title: Crash Cut
entries.text:
Crash Cut

Start inside the eventFlash-forward opening

A crash cut slams two images together with no blend, so the join itself stings. One side of the splice and the other collide; unlike a smash that breaks an earned quiet, a crash cut often starts inside the event or hits like a drum from the first frame.

Volume

Create this Crash Cut

Narrative function

A trunk, a man, a knife already in play, then the story will explain how we got here. Or a cymbal, a face, a rehearsal that never had a polite establishing wide.

The next image must hurt, and it must hurt immediately. Use it as percussion, as in medias res, as a refusal of the soft open.

It is the wrong tool when you have just built a hush that should be betrayed: that betrayal is a Smash Cut. It is the wrong tool when you only skip time in one seat: that is a Jump Cut.

A few frames of interrupt are a Flash Cut, not a committed new scene. Do not open on a sensation the rest of the story cannot causally earn.

How it works

Cut A to B with maximum difference in scale, brightness, or violence of content, and with no mix. Often B is already mid-action (a trunk, a gun, a kit).

Mark any later temporal reset clearly (a title, a younger haircut) so the crash is a structure, not an accident. Prompt: crash cut on [Subject], two images colliding with no polite blend, a hard join that should sting.

When to use it

Use it to open on the consequence, to hit a downbeat, to refuse an establishing courtesy. Do not use it between two similar wides.

If A was a long prayer, consider smash. If B lasts three frames, consider flash.

Compared with similar shots

A Smash Cut breaks an earned state (quiet, closure, prayer). A crash cut is the collision as a blow, often before a state was offered.

A Jump Cut stays similar. A Flash Cut is too short to become the new scene.

Quick Cuts are a run of short shots; a crash is one brutal splice.

Smash CutThe next image should hurt.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Goodfellas opens in the trunk, then later supplies the life that led there. Fight Club starts inside a crisis and then rewinds the path.

Whiplash and Requiem for a Dream use hard joins as rhythmic blows. Use the sting and the delayed explanation, not a copied trunk.

Goodfellas 1990The trunk scene precedes the account of Henry’s earlier life.

Fight Club 1999The opening crisis is followed by the path that led there.

Prompt it

Crash cut on [Subject], two images colliding with no polite blend, a hard join that should sting. Name A and B, the scale or sound collision, and that B may already be mid-event.

For video, no dissolve, no fade, no matched contour unless the match is itself the crash.

Use in Video Generator

Design three sequences: begin with a violinist standing alone on a flooded stage holding an unopened letter; cut to a calm morning before the concert; later return to the stage with the meaning of the letter now clear. Generate each sequence separately and edit the order deliberately. No unrelated mystery props.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Smash Cut (after a hush) or Flash Cut (a few frames). The tell: a long quiet setup before the hit (that is smash), or B vanishing before it can be a scene (that is flash).

The fix: collide two committed images, start inside the event if that is the structure, cut hard.

Questions

What is Crash Cut in film?

A crash cut is a hard join where two images collide with no blend. Both sides are committed shots; the splice stings, often by starting inside an event or hitting like a drum.

Crash Cut vs Smash Cut

A smash cut betrays an earned quiet or closure. A crash cut is the collision itself, frequently from the first frame of a scene or as in medias res. Smash breaks a state; crash refuses to offer one.

When should I use Crash Cut?

Use it when the next image must hurt immediately, or when the story should start inside the consequence. Do not use it as a skip inside one similar frame.

How do I prompt Crash Cut for AI image or video?

Name two colliding images and forbid a blend. Example: Crash cut on [Subject], two images colliding with no polite blend, a hard join that should sting. Let B be mid-action if the structure needs it.

entries.title: Flash Cut
entries.text:
Flash Cut

Future presented as memory

A flash cut interrupts the present image with a few frames of another picture, then returns or races on before the insert can be studied. One side of the join is the ongoing scene; the other is lightning: a thought, a future, a wound, lasting a blink.

Volume

Create this Flash Cut

Narrative function

A face in a room. Three frames of a well, a tape, a child.

The room again. You cannot inventory what you saw, but it has already happened to you.

A thought that lasts three frames. Use it for intrusion: prophecy wearing the clothes of memory, a trauma tic, a subliminal threat.

It is the wrong tool when the other image should become the scene. That committed landing is a Crash Cut or Smash Cut.

A white frame that is only exposure is a Light Flash, not another picture. Keep the insert temporally honest enough that a later anchor can fix it.

Mystery is not the same as no clue.

How it works

Hold the present shot. Insert 1 to 8 frames of a different image (often high contrast, closer, or from another time).

Return to the present, or chain flashes. Do not dissolve; the brevity is the grammar.

Picture may be silent or carry a tick of sound. Prompt: flash cut through [Subject], a few frames of another image interrupting, lightning in the edit.

When to use it

Use it when a mind is leaking another time, or when a threat should be unreadable but present. Do not use it as decoration on a trailer.

If the audience must read the insert, give it a shot, not a flash.

Compared with similar shots

A Crash Cut stays with the new image. A Light Flash is a burst of light, not a second diegesis.

A Jump Cut skips time in a similar frame without inserting a foreign picture. Smash Cut commits to contrast as the new present.

Flash cut is an interrupt.

Crash CutThe next image must hurt.

Light FlashA cut that is also a wound of light.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

The Ring uses stolen frames as contamination. Natural Born Killers sprays interruptive images as a nervous system.

Arrival presents images that first read as memory and are later re-placed in time. Use the brevity and the later anchor, not a copied well.

Arrival 2016Images initially read as memories are later understood in a different temporal relation.

Prompt it

Flash cut through [Subject], a few frames of another image interrupting, lightning in the edit. Name the present scene, the insert (and its duration in frames), and the return.

For video, no dissolve, no long hold on the insert. If the insert is only white, you asked for a light flash.

Use in Video Generator

Show brief intimate images of a woman teaching a child to repair a radio, initially without dates or age labels. In the present, she has never met the child. A later encounter reveals these are future moments. Generate stable radio and room details that make the temporal recognition precise.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Light Flash (no second image) or Crash Cut (the insert stays). The tell: a white blink, or a new scene that never returns to the present.

The fix: a countable handful of frames of a different picture, then the original scene, hard cuts.

Questions

What is Flash Cut in film?

A flash cut inserts a few frames of another image into an ongoing shot. One side is the present; the other is a blink of a different picture, too short to become the scene.

Flash Cut vs Crash Cut

A crash cut lands in a new committed image. A flash cut interrupts and (usually) returns. Duration is the difference: a scene versus a handful of frames.

When should I use Flash Cut?

Use it for a thought, a leak of another time, or a threat too brief to inventory. Do not use it when the other image needs to be read as the new present.

How do I prompt Flash Cut for AI image or video?

Name the present shot, the insert, and the frame count. Example: Flash cut through [Subject], a few frames of another image interrupting. Hard cuts, no dissolve, then return.
