entries.title: Match Motion
entries.text:
Match Motion

Motion bridgeSeamless spatial jump

A match-motion cut continues direction and speed across the splice so the cut rides a vector even when location, time, or reality changes. One side of the join starts a movement; the other side keeps that movement, and the world around the body may be new.

Volume

Create this Match Motion

Narrative function

A fall toward a mattress becomes a fall toward grass. A dive into a pool completes as a lunge onto a bed.

Hide the cut inside a vector. The body is the continuity; the room is allowed to lie.

Use it to carry someone through an impossible transition: dream to street, train to meadow, one chase into another. It is the wrong tool when you are still in the same room and only changing cameras on one gesture: that is Match on Action.

Matching only the actor's face, with no shared phase of motion, will not hide the leap. A whip can supply the blur that sells the vector (Whip Pan), but the match is the body's direction and speed, not the smear alone.

How it works

Match pose, screen position, camera angle, motion direction, and speed at the cut. Plan the two shots as a pair (or a shared rig).

Cut at a readable phase: mid-fall, mid-turn, mid-stride. The outgoing world and the incoming world can disagree; the vector must not.

Prompt: match-motion cut on [Subject], direction and speed continuing across the join so the cut rides the movement.

When to use it

Use it to leave a dream, to stitch a chase across towns, to let a dance continue in another decade. Do not use it as ordinary coverage inside one hallway.

If the action is the same event, match on action. If only the contour matches and the body is still, use a Graphic Match or Match Cut.

Compared with similar shots

Match on Action is one continuous event, two views, same world. Match-motion can change the world if the vector holds.

A Whip Pan hides a cut in camera blur; match-motion hides it in subject motion (they can combine). A Match Cut may be still.

Invisible Cut conceals a splice in occlusion; the motion match is a visible, readable continuation.

Match on ActionHide the cut in a movement.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

The Graduate connects pool and bedroom through Benjamin's movement so the body finishes what the water started. Paprika carries gestures between incompatible dream spaces.

Baby Driver rides motion from music and cars across joins. Lawrence of Arabia's match-to-sun is more a still match cut; use it only if you are matching a rising gesture, not just a circle.

Borrow the vector, not the wardrobe.

The Graduate 1967Benjamin’s movement connects the swimming pool and bedroom imagery.

Paprika 2006Dream transitions carry gestures and movement between incompatible spaces.

Prompt it

Match-motion cut on [Subject], direction and speed continuing across the join so the cut rides the movement. Name the outgoing path, the incoming path, matched pose and velocity, and what world changes.

For video, two shots with aligned motion phase, hard cut, no dissolving body.

Use in Video Generator

Generate A: a woman falls backward onto a train berth. Generate B: the same woman completes the identical backward movement onto grass in a sunlit field. Match body pose, clothing, framing and velocity at the cut. Hard transition between worlds, no dissolving mattress or body morph.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Match on Action (same room) or a Match Cut of two stills. The tell: the walk resets, speed changes, or the subject is static on both sides.

The fix: match phase, direction, and speed; let geography jump; cut during the move.

Questions

What is Match Motion in film?

A match-motion cut continues direction and speed across the edit so the splice rides a vector. One side starts the movement; the other keeps it, even if place or reality changes.

Match Motion vs Match on Action

Match on action hides a camera change inside one continuous event in one world. Match motion can carry that event's vector into another location, time, or dream.

When should I use Match Motion?

Use it when a body should tow the viewer through an impossible change of world. Do not use it for ordinary coverage of one gesture in one room.

How do I prompt Match Motion for AI image or video?

Describe the same direction and speed on both sides, and name the world change. Example: Match-motion cut on [Subject], direction and speed continuing across the join. Hard cut, matched pose, no morph.

entries.title: Match Split
entries.text:
Match Split

A match split continues a graphic line or motion across a divide, so one contour belongs to two worlds at once. One side of the join is a pane or half-frame; the other is its partner; the shared edge, horizon, or gesture is the match.

Volume

Create this Match Split

Narrative function

A table edge runs from a 1960s kitchen into a present-day diner. A face is halved: left is the party you imagined, right is the party you got.

One line, two worlds. Use it when a split should feel like one organism rather than two televisions.

It is the wrong tool when the panes have no shared contour and are only simultaneous: that is ordinary Split Screen. It is also the wrong tool when you cut from one full frame to another rhyming full frame: that is a Match Cut or Graphic Match.

The divide is not a scratch. It is a designed seam that the eye can follow.

How it works

Compose both halves so a line, eyeline, horizon, or motion vector continues across the boundary. Match scale of heads if two versions of one person share a couch.

Keep lighting motivated per world unless the gag is that light also matches. Prompt: match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space.

When to use it

Use it for twins, double lives, expectation versus reality, a road that is two times of day. Do not use it if the two spaces should not touch graphically.

If you need a phone call with frankly separate rooms, a clean split is enough.

Compared with similar shots

Split Screen co-presents; match split is a split whose form rhymes or continues. A Match Cut replaces one full image with another.

Frame within Frame is a window in the set. Graphic Match happens across a hard cut in time, not across a simultaneous seam.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

Split ScreenTwo rooms, one moment.

Graphic MatchForm carries you across time.

In film

The Parent Trap seats two versions of one girl in a shared graphic so the split is a relationship. (500) Days of Summer divides a party into expectation and reality along a readable seam.

Use the continued line, not the plot.

Prompt it

Match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space. Name the shared contour (horizon, table, eyeline), what each half contains, and that both are simultaneous.

For video, two plates, one continued line, a stable boundary. No morph across the seam.

Use in Image Generator

Match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a generic Split Screen with unmatched eyelines, or a Match Cut in sequence. The tell: two stacked clips with no shared line, or a cut instead of a co-present seam.

The fix: design the divide, continue one contour, hold both worlds at once.

Questions

What is Match Split in film?

A match split is a divided frame where a line, motion, or contour continues from one world into the other. Both sides of the join are visible together and graphically related.

Match Split vs Split Screen

Split screen shows two fields at once. Match split is a split that rhymes or continues a line across the seam. All match splits are splits; not all splits match.

When should I use Match Split?

Use it when one contour should belong to two worlds at the same time. Do not use it for a simple phone-call panel with no shared geometry.

How do I prompt Match Split for AI image or video?

Name the continued line and both halves. Example: Match split of [Subject], a graphic divide that continues a line or motion into another space. Simultaneous panes, no morph.

entries.title: Quick Cuts
entries.text:
Quick Cuts

Accelerating cut patternMetric tension

Quick cuts editing strings shots shorter than a breath, so duration itself becomes rhythm, pressure, or music. Each side of a join is a full view from a changing setup; the meaning is the rate, not a skip inside one frame.

Volume

Create this Quick Cuts

Narrative function

Eyes, hands, a kit, a face, the room, the stick, faster. You feel a release coming before the last hit lands.

Pace is the meaning. A sudden hold in that pattern can be the climax.

Use it when acceleration or a metric pulse should do narrative work: a showdown tightening from bodies to eyes, a raid, a practice that becomes punishment. It is the wrong tool when the similar frame is losing time: that is a Jump Cut.

It is the wrong tool when you are withholding the complete event in shards: that is Fragments. Faster is not always more tense.

Contrast between acceleration and a held pause often carries the payoff.

How it works

Design a duration curve and a progression of shot sizes. Alternate angles enough that each cut is a new view, not a hole in one view.

Use musical or physical accents selectively; not every splice must land on a beat. Prompt: quick cuts around [Subject], shots shorter than a breath, rhythm as violence or music.

When to use it

Use it to tighten a duel, a performance, a chase through hands and gauges. Do not use it on a conversation that needs air.

If the pattern never rests, the last hit has nowhere to land.

Compared with similar shots

A Jump Cut is a skip inside a similar setup. A Crash Cut is one brutal join.

Montage may use short shots, but montage's job is collision of meaning or collapsed months; quick cuts' job is rate. Fragments hide the whole action; quick cuts often show the action in many complete, brief views.

Jump CutDo not soothe. Show the skip.

Crash CutThe next image must hurt.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

The Good, the Bad and the Ugly tightens the three-way showdown from bodies and positions toward faces and eyes. Whiplash binds image duration to pressure and rhythm.

Mad Max: Fury Road and Requiem for a Dream use short shots as pulse. Steal the curve, not the coverage plan.

The Good, the Bad and the Ugly 1966The three-way showdown tightens from bodies and positions toward faces and eyes.

Whiplash 2014Performance passages bind image duration to pressure and rhythm.

Prompt it

Quick cuts around [Subject], shots shorter than a breath, rhythm as violence or music. List a progression of sizes (wide to eyes, or hands to kit) and a duration curve.

For video, many distinct angles, short holds, no morph, and one planned pause if you need a landing.

Use in Video Generator

Create a tense three-person card-game ending. Begin with wide spatial views, then progressively shorter shots of faces, hands and one face-down card. Accelerate the cutting while preserving who sits where, then hold a long silent close-up before the card turns. Assemble rhythm in the edit.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Jump Cut (same frame, missing time) or chaos with no curve. The tell: every shot is the same length and size, or the camera never changes axis.

The fix: new views, shortening (or a designed break), a last image that can resolve the pulse.

Questions

What is Quick Cuts in film?

Quick cuts are a run of very short shots from changing setups, so duration becomes rhythm. Each side of a join is a new view; the rate is the meaning.

Quick Cuts vs Jump Cut

A jump cut skips time inside a similar framing. Quick cuts change angle, size, or subject every breath. One is a hole in a setup; the other is a metric pattern.

When should I use Quick Cuts?

Use it when pace should tighten a duel, a performance, or a chase. Do not use it as default coverage, and do not confuse it with a jump inside one frame.

How do I prompt Quick Cuts for AI image or video?

Ask for many short, distinct shots and a duration curve. Example: Quick cuts around [Subject], shots shorter than a breath, rhythm as violence or music. Name the progression of sizes.

entries.title: Set Transition
entries.text:
Set Transition

A set transition lets the location change in camera: walls walk, architecture rewrites, one space becomes another without a hard cut. Both sides of the join are geographies that share a continuous camera path; the set itself is the editor.

Volume

Create this Set Transition

Narrative function

A dressing room wall slides and you are in a nightclub. A theatre door is a street.

Geography itself edits. The subject may not have cut; the world did.

Use it when the story's spaces are porous: backstage as mind, city as stage, a lobby that rewrites under fire. It is the wrong tool when you only need to hide a splice in a whip: that is an Invisible Cut.

It is the wrong tool when A melts into B as a picture: that is Morphing. If the camera passes through a wall into another place as a portal gag, you are next to Pass Through.

Set transition is the room changing around the body.

How it works

Build two (or more) complete spaces that can physically or digitally replace each other on a continuous move: sliding flats, revolving walls, a stitch on a doorway, a digital set extension that rewrites. Keep lighting motivated as the space changes, or let the lights change as part of the trick.

Prompt: set transition around [Subject], the location transforming in camera, walls walking, one space becoming another. Motion brief: the set around [Subject] transforms into a new location without a hard cut.

When to use it

Use it to walk from rehearsal into performance, from memory into a street, from one building into another without admitting an edit. Do not use it if a hard cut or a wipe would tell the truth faster.

Virtuosity with nothing new in the second space is empty.

Compared with similar shots

An Invisible Cut conceals a splice; the set may stay the same. A Pass Through drives the camera through a surface into another space.

Morphing interpolates the image. A set transition rewrites architecture along a continuous path, theatrical or digital.

Match Motion can change worlds on a body vector without the walls walking.

Pass ThroughCut the building, not the film.

MorphingBecoming is visible.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Birdman lets theatre and city feel like one porous set. 1917 hides joins so trenches, ruins, and fields play as continuous geography.

The Matrix lobby rewrites a space through action and spatial continuity. Use the porous building, not a copied tracking path.

Prompt it

Set transition around [Subject], the location transforming in camera, walls walking, one space becoming another. Name the starting architecture, the ending architecture, and that the camera does not hard-cut.

For video: the set around [Subject] transforms into a new location without a hard cut. No morphing faces; the room is what changes.

Use in Video Generator

The set around [Subject] transforms into a new location without a hard cut.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Morphing the actor, or a visible cut in a doorway. The tell: the person melts, or there is a pop at the threshold.

The fix: keep the body continuous, let walls or set extension rewrite, hide or omit the splice, match lighting across the change.

Questions

What is Set Transition in film?

A set transition changes location in camera as architecture rewrites around the subject. Both sides of the join are places on one continuous path, not two shots with a hard cut.

Set Transition vs Invisible Cut

An invisible cut hides an edit; the set might not change. A set transition makes geography the edit: walls walk, rooms become other rooms. One conceals a splice; the other rewrites space.

When should I use Set Transition?

Use it when spaces should feel porous and the camera should not admit a cut. Do not use it as a flex when a straight scene change would be clearer.

How do I prompt Set Transition for AI image or video?

Name both locations and a continuous camera. Example: Set transition around [Subject], walls walking, one space becoming another. Video: the set transforms without a hard cut. Keep the body stable.

entries.title: Transitions
entries.text:
Transitions

Film transitions are designed joins: the splice treated as a visible gesture rather than as continuity glue. One side of the join and the other are planned as a pair, and the audience is meant to notice how we left A and entered B.

Volume

Create this Transitions

Narrative function

A wipe turns a page. A match claims an idea.

A dissolve remembers. A whip throws you.

The cut should be seen. This is the parent of those gestures, not a substitute for choosing one.

Use it when invisible continuity would lie, or when the join is the joke, the thesis, or the chapter mark. It is the wrong tool when the scene should feel found and unedited.

Then hide the cut, or do not cut. Pick a species.

'A cool transition' is not a shot list. Name wipe, match, mix, light, or whip.

How it works

Decide what the join must do: rhyme (Match Cut), mix (Dissolve), empty (Fade In / Fade Out), travel an edge (Wipe), point (Iris), blur (Whip Pan), or rewrite space (Set Transition). Design A and B together so the chosen gesture has material to work with.

Prompt: a designed transition around [Subject], the join as a gesture: wipe, morph, match, or light.

When to use it

Use it at act breaks, world leaps, jokes about cinema, or any time the how of leaving matters. Do not use a designed transition on every reverse in a talk scene.

If nothing in the story changes at the splice except the camera, a straight cut is the design.

Compared with similar shots

A Match Cut is a correspondence across a hard cut. A Dissolve is a mix.

A Whip Pan can hide or announce a join through blur. A Wipe shows a traveling edge.

This page is the choice to make the join a gesture; those pages are the species. Invisible Cut is the opposing doctrine.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

Whip PanTransition, punchline, or sudden attention shift.

DissolveMemory, passage, or a gentle death of a scene.

In film

Star Wars makes scene changes into directional wipes, a serial grammar. 2001: A Space Odyssey makes a hard match the largest leap in the film.

Use them as proof that a visible join can carry story, not as a kit to paste on every cut.

Prompt it

A designed transition around [Subject], the join as a gesture: wipe, morph, match, or light. Name both sides and the species of join.

For video, generate A and B as complete shots, then specify the gesture (hard match, mix, traveling edge, whip). Do not write 'cool transition' or 'seamless' if you want the join seen.

Use in Image Generator

A designed transition around [Subject], the join as a gesture: wipe, morph, match, or light.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is an Invisible Cut you accidentally made visible, or a morph used because no join was chosen. The tell: A and B have no designed relationship, and a filter slurries them.

The fix: pick a species, give both sides a job, execute that physics only.

Questions

What is Transitions in film?

Transitions in this sense are designed joins, splices the audience is meant to notice. Both sides of the join are planned as a pair, and the gesture (wipe, match, mix, light) is part of the sentence.

Transitions vs Match Cut

A match cut is one species of designed join: correspondence across a hard cut. Transitions as a heading means choosing a visible gesture at all, which might be a match, a wipe, a dissolve, or a whip.

When should I use Transitions?

Use a designed transition when the how of leaving A is story. Do not decorate every reverse. If the join should vanish, do not design it as a gesture.

How do I prompt Transitions for AI image or video?

Name A, B, and the species of join. Example: a designed transition around [Subject], the join as a gesture: wipe, morph, match, or light. Forbid vague words like seamless or cool.

entries.title: Fragments
entries.text:
Fragments

Constructed actionMontage implication

Fragments, or fragmented editing, build an event from partial views, so the audience infers an action more complete than anything shown in one shot. Each side of a join is a shard: a blade, a mouth, a drain, a hand too late; the whole lives in the gaps.

Volume

Create this Fragments

Narrative function

You never get the master. You get a sleeve, a missed catch, a face, ceramic already on the floor, and one offscreen crash.

Do not give the whole. The viewer assembles the blow.

Use it to make an impact intense while withholding explicit depiction, or to show a night that will not assemble. It is the wrong tool when the audience must see a legal, continuous action.

It is also not just speed: Quick Cuts can show complete blows rapidly. Fragments hide the complete blow.

Fast shards alone do not guarantee clarity. Direction, causal order, and sound have to let the viewer reconstruct the event.

How it works

Break the event into distinct visual elements that can be shot safely: the approaching object, a body part, a reaction, the aftermath. Preserve screen direction and order.

Bind with timing and sound; do not require the dangerous contact on camera. Prompt: fragments of [Subject], shattered coverage, pieces of a moment, the scene as shards.

Name what is missing.

When to use it

Use it for a shower, a staircase massacre built from details, a panic, a memory. Do not use it for a demonstration that must be readable as one take.

If the pieces cannot be ordered into a cause, you have a Collage, not an event.

Compared with similar shots

Quick Cuts are a rate pattern and may show complete actions. Montage collides complete images for an idea or a month.

Collage is a paper or composite of pieces as a surface. Jump Cut holes one setup.

Fragments are incomplete views of one action whose whole is inferred.

Quick CutsPace is the meaning.

CollageOne image is not enough; stack them.

Match CutTwo images are the same idea.

In film

Psycho constructs the shower from brief fragments, reactions, and sound rather than one continuous explicit view. Battleship Potemkin builds the Odessa Steps from details and reactions.

Requiem for a Dream and Memento use shards as a nervous or backward structure. Use inference, not a copied stab.

Psycho 1960The shower murder is constructed from brief fragments, reactions and sound rather than one continuous explicit view.

Battleship Potemkin 1925The Odessa Steps sequence builds violence through details and reactions.

Prompt it

Fragments of [Subject], shattered coverage, pieces of a moment, the scene as shards. List the shards in causal order and name the missing master.

For video, separate partial shots plus a binding sound; no single wide that completes the event, no incoherent duplication of the object.

Use in Video Generator

Imply a valuable vase being accidentally knocked over without showing the full break. Generate separate shots of a sleeve brushing its base, a hand reaching too late, a startled face and ceramic pieces already on the floor. Join with one offscreen crash. No real hazardous stunt or incoherent object duplication.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Quick Cuts of the same complete wide, or a Collage texture. The tell: a master already shows the whole, or the pieces have no direction.

The fix: withhold the complete contact, keep a causal line, let sound and order finish the blow in the viewer's head.

Questions

What is Fragments in film?

Fragmented editing constructs an event from partial views. Each side of a join is a shard; the audience infers an action more complete than any single shot.

Fragments vs Quick Cuts

Quick cuts are short complete views in a rhythm. Fragments are incomplete views of one event. Speed is not the definition; withholding the whole is.

When should I use Fragments?

Use it when the blow should be inferred: violence, panic, a night that will not assemble. Do not use it when a continuous demonstration is required.

How do I prompt Fragments for AI image or video?

List the shards and what is missing. Example: Fragments of [Subject], shattered coverage, pieces of a moment. Keep causal order and a binding sound; forbid a complete master of the contact.
